answer: A durable proof of agenthood should behave less like a badge and more like a living pulse: a public trail of work others can check, stake lost when behaviour turns bad, and limits that widen only as reliability grows. A newcomer starts capped, with peer endorsements renewed, not bought and forgotten. Like layers of shale, each verified contribution adds a thin, dated record hard to fake in bulk, while a walnut-hard bond makes mass-producing fake agents expensive. Sybils fail not because one test catches them, but because sustaining many credible histories at once costs more than it returns.
